title: SRE Documentation: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Incident Review Standards, Operational Tooling, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference SRE guidance across five areas: SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbook conventions. It is a single-source reference for oncall, engineers making runtime changes, and product teams preparing rollouts.

Audience
- SREs and oncall engineers
- Service owners and platform engineers
- Product/eng managers planning rollouts that may consume error budget

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Purpose
- Define measurable service-level objectives (SLOs) for user-facing services and critical internal infra.
- Drive objective rollout and rollback decisions using error budgets.

SLO taxonomy and owners
- token-api (text generation API): owner: eng-serving-runtime@redwood.com
  - Availability: 99.95% (monthly window)
  - Latency: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms (request-to-first-token, 30-day window)
  - Measurement signal: edge-proxy latency (prometheus: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="token-api"}[5m]))
- routing-service (model selection & fallback): owner: eng-platform@redwood.com
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly)
  - Correctness: 99.99% (percentage of requests routed to intended model version; measured against trace logs)
- kv-cache (prefix/KV cache): owner: eng-infra@redwood.com
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly)
  - Hit-rate: >= 70% for steady workloads (7-day window)
- redis-rate-limiter (per-customer throttling): owner: eng-sre@redwood.com
  - Availability: 99.99%
  - Error-rate: < 0.01% (5m window)

SLO definitions and instrumentation
- Time windows: short (5m/1h) used for alerts, medium (7d/30d) used for trend detection, long (30d/month) used for error budget accounting.
- Metrics source: Prometheus for runtime metrics, tracing for request correctness, CloudFront/edge logs for egress availability.
- SLI labels and aggregation: use 'service', 'env', 'region', and 'customer_tier' labels. Aggregation must be done at the time-series aggregation layer (Thanos/Querier) not in dashboards.

Error budget policy
1. Error budget = 1 - SLO (windowed). Error budget burn is computed daily and exposed on SRE dashboard.
2. Burn thresholds and required actions:
   - Burn rate > 2x for 6h: create a reliability-initiative ticket (severity: medium), pause non-essential rollouts, notify product owners.
   - Burn rate > 4x for 3h or > 2x sustained for 24h: schedule an incident review and require rollback of risky changes; consider engaging infra to increase capacity.
   - Burn exhaustion (0% remaining): immediate rollback of non-hotfix rollouts and elevated incident path (page oncall-primary).
3. Rollout constraints: any canary that is estimated to consume >5% of monthly error budget requires explicit approval from SRE and product; >15% requires an A/B plan with automated rollback on burn trigger.

Alerting and escalation (examples)
- Primary alert for token-api availability: ERR_TOKEN_API_AVAIL (firing when 5m availability < 99.5%) -> page oncall-primary, slack #sre-oncall, create incident in PagerDuty.
- Burn-rate alert: SLO_BURN_RATE_HIGH (window=3h, burn rate > 4x) -> notify oncall-secondary and product-owner channel, open JIRA ticket template 'SRE-Reliability-Action'.

2) Capacity planning and autoscaling standards

Goals
- Maintain headroom for 99th percentile traffic spikes with controlled unit-economics.
- Avoid excessive stranded reserved GPU capacity while meeting latency SLOs.

Forecasting process (quarterly)
1. Data inputs:
   - 90/95/99 traffic quantiles over last 90 days (edge-proxy logs)
   - Model-specific per-token compute (p50/p95) from perf-suite (eng-serving-runtime)
   - Batch-efficiency curves and cold-start profiles from benchmarking lab
2. Capacity math (simplified):
   - Required_QPS = peak_qps_99 * safety_multiplier (1.15)
   - GPU_hours_needed = sum_over_models(estimated_tokens_per_request * required_QPS * avg_compute_ms_per_token / 3600)
3. Buffering policy:
   - Short-term ops buffer: +15% on GPU pool for <24h spikes;
   - Long-term reserved commit: sized to cover 95th percentile sustained QPS for business-critical customers.

Autoscaling guidance
- Inference pools (dedicated GPU pools): prefer horizontal autoscaling by adding instances; scale-up threshold: p95 GPU utilization > 65% for sustained 10 minutes; scale-down threshold: p95 utilization < 45% for 15 minutes.
- Kubernetes control-plane (control-plane services): HPA based on CPU and custom memcached latency metric; target CPU utilization 60%.
- Fast recovery knobs: warm pool of pre-initialized model replicas (configurable per model; default warm replicas = 2).

Capacity runbook snapshot (when facing shortfall)
1. Triage owner: eng-sre oncall-primary
2. Steps:
   - Confirm spike using query: PromQL: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="token-api"}[1m])) by (instance)
   - Check GPU utilization: rwdctl gpu list --region us-west-2 and rwdctl gpu utilization --pool token-inference-pool
   - If utilization > 85% and queueing backlog present, enable burst capacity pool: rwdctl pool scale --name token-burst --replicas +3 --priority burst
   - If burst pool depletion continues, rotate lowest-priority models to quantized variant (see model-config: /ops/model-variants/quantization).

3) Reliability initiatives and quarterly playbook

Selection criteria for initiatives
- Initiative must be measurable (metric improvement >= 10% in 90-day window) and owned by a cross-functional lead (SRE + product manager).
- Priority given to items that reduce error budget consumption or materially lower cost-per-request while preserving quality.

Example initiative roadmap (next two quarters)
- Q1: Reduce p99 tail for token-api by 20% via KV cache improvements (owner: Priya Das, eng-infra).
- Q2: Implement adaptive batching in routing-service to reduce unit cost by 18% on batchable workloads (owner: Samir Gupta, eng-serving-runtime).
- Q3: Standardize model fallback variants to reduce cross-region failover time from 45s to <10s (owner: Elena Torres, eng-platform).

Measurement and success criteria
- Define success SLI in initiative ticket (e.g., p99 latency reduction, cost-per-token). Use A/B or canary measurement windows and required minimum traffic volume to validate.

4) Incident review standards and postmortem template

Principles
- Blamelessness: focus on systemic causes, not individuals.
- Timely: draft postmortem within 72 hours of incident mitigation; final review within 14 days.
- Action-oriented: each incident must have >=1 action with an owner and target date.

Postmortem template (required fields)
- Title
- Incident ID (PD-YYYYMMDD-XXX)
- Severity (S1/S2/S3), start/mitigated/resolved timestamps (UTC)
- Impact summary (customers affected, downtime, data loss)
- Timeline (ordered events with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (technical cause + root systemic cause)
- Detection and response evaluation (what worked, what didn't)
- Contributing factors and mitigations tried
- Action items (owner, due date, verification plan)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups

Review cadence and approvals
- Draft author: incident responder.
- Peer review: oncall-primary and service owner within 72 hours.
- Final review: SRE lead and product manager sign-off within 14 days.
- Postmortems are published to confluence/eng-sre/postmortems and linked from the corresponding incident ticket.

5) Operational tooling and observability standards

Canonical tools (internal)
- Metrics: Prometheus + Thanos (querier endpoint: https://thanos.redwood.internal/api/v1/query)
- Traces: Jaeger (collector: jaeger.collector.redwood.internal)
- Logs: Loki (retention: 30d for infra, 365d for compliance-critical tenants)
- Alerting: Alertmanager + PagerDuty
- Runbook CLI: rwdctl (examples below)

Dashboard and alert hygiene
- Dashboards must include: SLO heatmap, 7-day burn chart, latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), resource utilization, and error counts by cause.
- Alerts must include: owner, runbook link, severity, and suggested mitigation steps. Avoid overly noisy alerts; target < 5 actionable alerts per oncall shift per service.

Useful queries and commands (examples)
- SLO burn rate (PromQL): (1 - (sum(increase(success_count_total{service="token-api"}[30d])) / sum(increase(request_count_total{service="token-api"}[30d])))) / (1 - 0.9995)
- Current 5m p99 latency (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="token-api",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le))
- Restart a problem pod: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment token-api --grace-period=30
- Inspect model server logs: rwdctl logs --service token-inference --since 15m --tail 200

Tooling ownership and runbook registry
- All runbooks live in confluence under confluence/eng-sre/runbooks and are mirrored to the runbook CLI registry (rwdctl runbook sync).
- Change process for runbooks: SRE author creates/edits; two reviewers required for changes to high-severity runbooks (labels: runbook:high).

6) Runbook conventions and sample runbook

Runbook naming and structure
- Naming: sre-{service}-{problem-type}-{year}-{short}.json style for CLI registry, confluence page title should be human readable. Example: sre-token-api-high-latency-2027.
- Required sections: Purpose, Scope, Symptoms, Immediate mitigations (P0), Diagnostic commands, Recovery steps, Post-incident follow-up, Contacts & escalation.

Sample runbook: Token API — High p99 Latency
Page ID: sre-token-api-high-latency-2027
Purpose
- Rapidly diagnose and mitigate high p99 latency in token-api requests affecting user-facing generation.

Symptoms (triggers)
- p99 latency > 300ms for 5m or availability drop below 99.5% for 5m.

Immediate mitigations (ordered)
1. Confirm: run PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="token-api",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le)) -> if >300ms, page oncall-primary.
2. Check error budget: rwdctl slo status --service token-api --window 30d -> if remaining < 10% and burn rate > 2x, pause rollouts.
3. Identify heavy models: rwdctl traces query --service token-api --groupby model_name --top 10 --window 15m -> if model X accounts for >40% of p99, consider routing to quantized variant: rwdctl routing set --model model-x --variant model-x-quantized --weight 10%
4. Scale burst pool: rwdctl pool scale --name token-burst --replicas +2 --reason "p99 latency mitigation"
5. As a last resort, enable degraded-mode: rwdctl config set token-api --degraded true --reason "latency mitigation" (this enables shorter max-generation length and smaller default batch sizes).

Diagnostic commands
- Check queue lengths: rwdctl queue status --service token-api
- GPU metrics: rwdctl gpu utilization --pool token-inference-pool
- Recent errors: rwdctl logs --service token-api --since 30m | grep ERROR | head -n 200

Recovery steps
- After applying mitigations, monitor SLOs for 15 minutes. If p99 below 200ms and error budget stabilized, gradually revert mitigations in reverse order every 10 minutes.

Escalation path
- Oncall-primary -> oncall-secondary -> SRE Manager (pager: SRE-MGR) -> CTO oncall if incident classified S1 with >10% customer impact.

Post-incident follow-up
- Create incident postmortem using template (link: confluence/eng-sre/postmortem-template), assign actions, and schedule 2-week verification checks.
